minutes.headline: Committee held off on a bus-application deadline policy, waived two reads, passed lunch policies and approved ESSER transfers.
minutes.summary: The committee heard public comment on SEL and the equity audit, got an FY24 budget update from the business manager, and debated first and second reads of policies. The transportation policy's rights-waiver language was not ready, so it was sent back for legal review. The committee approved the ESSER SR2/SR3 transfers, two lunch policies, the extended day and ELC handbooks, and a letter supporting ARPA funds for Marshall Park.

public_comment.topic: Responded to committee statements on transportation sign-up, equity auditors, mandatory SEL and research on SEL; asked each member to define equity.

what_happened.line: The School Committee did not give the transportation policy a second reading and sent its revised variants to attorney review through the policy subcommittee.
The committee did not waive first reading of the budget transfer authority policy (3105), though it waived first reading of the other listed policies.
Members favored posting line item transfers on the business manager's web page ahead of meetings.
Third reading of the insufficient-funds and meal-charging lunch policies passed; votes on the ESSER transfers and extended day handbooks were not audible.
The business manager gave an FY24 budget update covering health insurance, state aid, circuit breaker and free lunch funding, with the total still not final.

why_it_matters: The FY24 school budget total was still moving at this meeting, so the figure residents will be asked to vote on had not been set.

The transportation policy, which governs how families sign up for buses, stays unfinished until the legal review comes back, and the transfer authority policy will get a first reading, which sets how freely the district can move money between lines during the year.
